speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes, specifically how long they last and if there is any post-episode confusion? Have you noticed any specific triggers, such as stress, lack of sleep, or flashing lights, that precede these events?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of head trauma or neurological conditions, and is there any family history of epilepsy? I would also like to know if these episodes occur during sleep or exclusively while he is awake.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: EEG: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side. Brain MRI: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The EEG findings of right temporal lobe spikes, combined with the aura of a muddy taste and automatisms like hand gestures, strongly suggest focal seizures. I have enough information to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
